look_here_first: LOOK BELOW THE LEAVES: a prostrate rooting mat of alternate, entire, kidney-shaped leaves on thin petioles. Look for tawny silky hairs (especially underneath). Find a tiny PALE, 5-lobed flower and trace its VERY SHORT flower/fruit stalk: the upper end hooks sharply DOWNWARD (recurved), not just a drooping leaf stalk. At maturity compare fruit (3–4 mm) with its persistent five sepals (~2.9–3.8 mm). Larger leaves alone are NOT enough to separate this species from Carolina ponyfoot.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Creeping perennial rooting at nodes; dense low mat, leaves held above shallow/subterranean creeping stolons.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Blades round to kidney-shaped with a conspicuous basal notch, entire/wavy edges, several basal radiating palmate veins; ALTERNATE on runners.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Stems and lower leaf surfaces conspicuously tawny silky-hairy (sericeous), often more hairy underneath than on upper surface.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Single tiny pale-green to white cup/funnel flower, five corolla lobes, from an axil; look UNDER leaves, not for showy morning-glory trumpets.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: CRITICAL: the upper end of the short pedicel hooks/recurves downward near the calyx. Photograph the entire attached stalk, not a fallen fruit.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Five rather broadly rounded, overlapping, persistent sepals (2.9–3.8 mm in fruit per FNA) typically shorter to barely longer than the mature 3–4 mm fruit.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruit a 2-lobed hairy capsule with fragile wall and separating lobes; do NOT confuse the sepals with flower petals.

key_traits.label: Growth habit
key_traits.text: Perennial, clonal creeping mat in gravelly oak woodland, disturbed sites, lakeshore margins; often only a few centimeters high aboveground. Roots form at nodes; perennial slender stolons commonly shallow or just below soil surface.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Alternate, not opposite; one leaf per node along creeping shoot (dense nodes may give a paired appearance).

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Rounded/reniform blades with cordate basal notch and entire or subtly wavy margins; palmate veins 5–7 in local Williamson flora. FNA typical 20–30 mm long and 30–40 mm wide, with broad individual ranges; a local UT Williamson account measured smaller material (<5–23 x <10–30 mm). Do not require a rigid cutoff.

key_traits.label: Leaf surface
key_traits.text: Silky tawny hairs on stems, more dense beneath the blade and on margins, sparse on upper leaf face. Inspect with hand lens; leaf hair is supporting, not exclusive, identification.

key_traits.label: Petiole
key_traits.text: Long relative to small hidden inflorescences. Flora of North America reports 20–170 mm including long extremes; UT Williamson County flora measured roughly 10–35 mm on local material.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Tiny, solitary to paired axillary flowers; five broad lobes of a fused pale-green or creamy-white funnel/cup corolla, approximately 3.1–4 mm FNA (local measured examples can be smaller). Persistent, five-lobed calyx outside corolla.

key_traits.label: Pedicel
key_traits.text: FNA: 5–13 mm, conspicuously recurved near tip. UT Williamson: very short, hooked and downward-pointing, increasing toward fruit, to roughly 12 mm; photograph the full pedicel and whether the curve is immediately below flower.
